_provenance.primary_source: ADF&G Division of Commercial Fisheries — Pacific Herring Annual Management Reports (PWS & SEAK)
secondary_sources: Exxon Valdez Oil Spill Trustee Council — Herring Injury Assessment
_provenance.notes: Alaska Pacific Herring (Clupea pallasii) support three distinct commercial fisheries: (1) Sac-roe herring (female roe — kazunoko — exported to Japan), (2) food/bait herring, and (3) spawn-on-kelp (SOK). The 1989 Exxon Valdez oil spill in Prince William Sound (PWS) caused catastrophic herring recruitment failure — the PWS herring stock collapsed from 100,000 mt biomass (1989) to below 10,000 mt (1993), eliminating the $12M annual sac-roe fishery. The stock has never fully recovered. PWS herring are listed as an Exxon Valdez injured resource not yet recovered.
